questions.question: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) was strategically designed to accelerate India’s long-term growth by prioritizing which of the following sectors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heavy industries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan**, which operated from **1956 to 1961**, was primarily based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, formulated by the renowned Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
• The core objective of this plan was to achieve **rapid industrialization** by shifting the economic focus from agriculture to the development of **basic and heavy industries**.
 
• It emphasized the production of **capital goods**, such as machinery and equipment, which were considered essential for building a self-reliant and sustainable industrial foundation for the **Indian economy**.
 
• During this period, the government established three major **steel plants** with foreign collaboration: **Bhilai** (with USSR assistance), **Durgapur** (with UK assistance), and **Rourkela** (with West German assistance).
 
• The plan also aligned with the **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**, which aimed to establish a **socialistic pattern of society** by giving the **Public Sector** a dominant role in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Strategy**:

 
 
• This economic strategy prioritized the **heavy industry sector** to ensure long-term growth, even if it meant slower growth in consumer goods in the short term.
 
• It was inspired by the industrialization patterns observed in the **Soviet Union**.
 
 
 
• **Village-level artisan development**:
 
 
• While the plan focused on heavy industries, the **Karve Committee** (Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee) in **1955** suggested that small-scale industries should also be promoted to ensure rural employment.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the First Plan**:
 
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)** was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model** and focused on **agriculture**, irrigation, and power to stabilize the economy after independence.
 
 
 
• **Key Organizations**:
 
 
• The **Atomic Energy Commission** was headed by **Homi J. Bhabha** during this era, and the **Tata Institute of Fundamental Research** was expanded to boost scientific research.

questions.question: Keshab Chandra Sen was a prominent leader of which of the following reform movements in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen** joined the **Brahmo Samaj** in **1857** and was later appointed its **Acharya** by **Debendranath Tagore** in **1862**.
 
• He was a radical reformer who played a pivotal role in internationalizing the movement and spreading its message beyond **Bengal** to the **Bombay** and **Madras** Presidencies.
 
• Under his leadership, the movement focused heavily on **women education**, **remarriage of widows**, and the abolition of **caste distinctions**.
 
• In **1866**, following ideological differences with **Debendranath Tagore** regarding radical social reforms and the inclusion of non-Hindu scriptures, Sen broke away to form the **Brahmo Samaj of India**.
 
• His efforts were central to the passing of the **Native Marriage Act of 1872** (also known as the **Civil Marriage Act**), which sought to curb **child marriage** and legalize **inter-caste marriages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**:

 
 
• Founded in **1867** in **Bombay** by **Atmaram Pandurang**.
 
• It was deeply inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj** and became a platform for social reform under **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade**.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj**:
 
 
• Established by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in **1875** in **Bombay**.
 
• It promoted the slogan **'Go back to the Vedas'** and focused on **Suddhi** (purification) movements and **monotheism**.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission**:
 
 
• Founded by **Swami Vivekananda** in **1897** at **Belur Math** near **Calcutta**.
 
• The organization is dedicated to **humanitarian relief** and social work, following the philosophy of **Ramakrishna Paramahansa**.

questions.question: Which major operation did the Indian government launch in May 2025 following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Sindoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Sindoor** was a major counter-terrorism offensive launched by the **Indian Government** and **Security Forces** in **May 2025**.
 
• The operation was a direct tactical response to a significant **terrorist attack** that occurred in **Pahalgam**, located in the **Anantnag district** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• The primary objective was to neutralize **infiltrators** and destroy **terrorist infrastructure** embedded in the rugged terrain of the **Lidder Valley** and surrounding **Himalayan ridges**.
 
• The mission involved a high degree of coordination between the **Indian Army**, **Para Special Forces**, and the **Jammu and Kashmir Police**, utilizing **real-time satellite intelligence** and **drone surveillance**.
 
• It aimed to restore security for the **Amarnath Yatra** route and ensure the safety of the local population and tourists in the **Kashmir Valley**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Significant Indian Operations**:

 
 
• **Operation Shakti**: This refers to the second series of **nuclear tests** conducted by India at the **Pokhran** range in **May 1998**, establishing India as a **nuclear-armed state**.
 
• **Operation Vijay**: The codename for the military action taken by India during the **1999 Kargil War** to evict **Pakistani regular soldiers** and **insurgents** from the **Line of Control (LoC)**.
 
• **Operation Trident**: An offensive operation by the **Indian Navy** during the **1971 Indo-Pakistani War**, which involved a devastating attack on the **Karachi Port** on the night of **December 4-5**.

questions.question: The provision of 'Single citizenship' for all in the Indian Constitution is adopted from the constitution of which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Constitution** provides for **Single Citizenship**, which means that every Indian citizen owes allegiance only to the Union of India, regardless of the state in which they reside.
 
• This provision is borrowed from the **British Constitution** (United Kingdom) to promote **fraternity** and **national integration** by removing barriers between different states.
 
• In contrast to the **United States of America**, which follows a system of **dual citizenship** (national and state), India opted for a unified citizenship to maintain the **unity and integrity** of the nation.
 
• The provisions regarding citizenship are enshrined in **Part II** of the **Constitution of India**, covering **Articles 5 to 11**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other features borrowed from the **British Constitution**:

 
 
• **Parliamentary form of government** and the **Rule of Law**.
 
• **Legislative procedure** and **Bicameralism**.
 
• **Cabinet System** and **Prerogative Writs**.
 
 
 
• Features from the **US Constitution**:
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights** and **Judicial Review**.
 
• **Independence of the Judiciary** and **Preamble**.
 
• **Impeachment of the President** and removal of judges.
 
 
 
• Features from the **Canadian Constitution**:
 
 
• **Federation with a strong Centre** and **Residuary Powers** vested in the Centre.
 
• **Advisory jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• Features from the **Australian Constitution**:
 
 
• **Concurrent List** and **Freedom of trade and commerce**.
 
• **Joint sitting** of the two Houses of Parliament.
